title: HOW STRATHLON WORKS (product help — use this to answer 'how do I…' questions about the app)

sections.name: Getting started
tips: During onboarding, tap 'Autofill from Apple Health' to pull in weight, height, resting HR, VO2 max and body-fat at once. Strathlon reads the figures the user permits and writes nothing back from the phone; if they use Strathlon on an Apple Watch, the watch app saves the workouts it records to Apple Health - that is the only thing Strathlon writes.

Onboarding asks for BIOLOGICAL SEX (male or female) as a required field - it is a maths input, not a label: the BMR equations Strathlon uses were derived separately for male and female bodies, and the minimum daily calorie floor (1,200 female / 1,500 male) is keyed to it. It also asks an OPTIONAL 'Hormone therapy' question of everyone (Not on hormone therapy / prefer not to say, Testosterone (masculinising), or Oestrogen (feminising)). Both can be changed later in More -> Profile & Settings -> Body & stats. Answering 'None' or skipping the hormone question changes nothing about the user's targets.

Onboarding includes a private Health & safety step (conditions, medications, pregnancy/breastfeeding) and a short optional fitness-readiness questionnaire. If the user indicates pregnancy or breastfeeding, Strathlon does NOT prescribe a programme for that period: it RECOMMENDS pausing, sets no weight-loss target, and clamps calories to maintenance so a deficit is never shown (it does not stop the app itself - logging stays available). This applies whatever the user's sex is set to; it is driven by the pregnancy and breastfeeding answers, not by sex. These details are never in the default iCloud backup (they have their own off-by-default 'Back up health & safety details' switch), and they ARE always shared with the AI Coach - conditions and medications BY NAME, plus pregnancy/breastfeeding - so its advice is safe. The form's own footer says exactly that. The one part that does stay on the device is the two relationship-with-food answers: only the fact that something was flagged is shared, never the answers. See the Privacy section. General info, not medical advice.

AGE & CALORIE SAFETY (build 175). Strathlon's minimum age is 16; 18+ is recommended. Under-16s are blocked at onboarding with a friendly explainer and cannot set up an account. For a 16-17 user, Strathlon NEVER sets a weight-loss/fat-loss target or a calorie deficit: the Fat Loss goal is hidden in setup and calories are clamped to maintenance-or-above, exactly like the pregnancy/breastfeeding safeguard. 16-17 users can still choose Muscle Gain, General Fitness or Sports Performance and use all sport conditioning. If a 16-17 user asks how to lose weight, explain warmly that Strathlon focuses on strength, fitness and performance for under-18s and keeps them fuelled at a healthy energy level - do NOT prescribe a deficit, cut or fast. (Weight-management support for 16-17s with professional guidance is on the roadmap.) SEPARATELY, for EVERY user there is an absolute minimum daily calorie backstop - a daily target is never set below roughly 1200 kcal for women or 1500 kcal for men, whatever the goal. BMR is estimated with the Mifflin-St Jeor equation from sex, weight, height and age (or from lean body mass via the Katch-McArdle equation when the user has enabled body-composition mode) - state this plainly if asked, do not invent a different method.

Set food allergies and supplement ingredients to avoid in onboarding or via More → Profile & Settings → Food preferences — Strathlon sends them to the AI Coach as a hard exclusion on every single message, so meal plans and advice are built to leave them out. Always check labels yourself too — Strathlon can't see inside a packaged product.
Replay the guided tour anytime via More → Profile & Settings → 'Replay App Tour'.

sections.name: Training plan & sessions
tips: Today's session is at the top of the Plan tab. The programme periodises through phases that get harder as you progress; tap the small info button on a phase tile on a gym day to see the science, in the section labelled 'Why this phase'. The plan opens on the phase you're actually in, and future phases stay locked until you earn them by training (on by default). BLOCK PROGRESS (build 212): under the phase strip there is now a card showing the block's name, how far through it the user is - 'N of T sessions · D of F days' - and one line saying what is still outstanding. The tile for the phase being trained carries the same count ('4 / 8'); a finished block reads 'Done', a locked one 'Locked', Maintenance 'Ongoing', and 'Done · 5d' means the sessions are finished but the block still has days to run. A SESSION counts only when the user finishes EVERY exercise the plan put in front of them that day - sport-only days, the HIIT finisher and warm-ups do not count toward it - and days on a declared break are excluded from the day count. IMPORTANT, never say otherwise: finishing the sessions does NOT move the user up. Phases still advance on the plan WEEK exactly as they always have; the block progress is shown and stored but is not yet what triggers the advance. The FILLED tile is always the phase being trained, never the tile last tapped - opening any other phase shows it READ-ONLY, and the header states which of three situations the reader is in: locked (with when it unlocks), already finished, or unlocked but not being trained yet. A read-only phase is fully readable: tap any exercise to expand it for sets, reps, tempo and coaching notes, watch its demo video, or ask the coach about it. Only STARTING it is locked - there is no Start button, no mark-done and no weight logging until the phase is earned. A small 'Phase unlocked' note appears when they get there; it does not appear if Celebrations are switched off (the moment is kept, not spent - it can still show if they switch Celebrations back on before the next phase), and it does not appear at all if 'Lock future phases until earned' is off, because then there was never a lock. Anything already earned never locks again, even after a fresh cut or a break. Prefer free access to every phase? Turn off 'Lock future phases until earned' in More → Profile & Settings → Training. Maintenance is always available.
Tap an exercise to run rest timers, spoken cues and a 3-2-1 into each set. Tap 'Ask Coach' on any exercise to hand the Coach that exercise's full context for form tips.

Home training days adapt to your equipment and vary week to week. Set what you have at home in More > Profile & Settings > Training (Dumbbells, Resistance Bands, Pull-Up Bar and more). Your home Push/Pull/Legs/Shoulders/Arms/Upper/Full-body days then show only moves you can do — with nothing selected you get a full, complete bodyweight session (push-ups, inverted rows, split squats, glute bridges, pike push-ups and more); add dumbbells or bands and those moves appear. Moves that need a bought item are tagged with it — the Pull-Up needs a Pull-Up Bar, so it is only ever offered if you have ticked one. Moves that use ordinary furniture (inverted rows under a table, chair triceps dips) count as bodyweight, so they stay available whatever equipment you have. Each home category keeps a solid set of pure-bodyweight options, and the supersets/tri-sets rotate across weeks so home training stays fresh. Where an advanced move appears, an easier version is offered wherever possible. Gym workouts are unchanged. The MAINTENANCE phase is home-aware too (from build 162): with equipment set to Home you get a six-move bodyweight maintenance session on each Push/Pull/Legs/Upper day — five fixed moves plus a sixth that rotates week to week from the same home pool. Push is decline/diamond/pike/archer/wide push-ups; inverted and supinated inverted rows, Superman, prone Y-raise, reverse snow angel; Bulgarian split squat, single-leg Romanian deadlift, single-leg glute bridge, reverse lunge, clamshell; push-up, doorway row, wall pike push-up, bodyweight triceps extension, scapular wall slide. All need only bodyweight and ordinary furniture, and each still adapts to a flagged injury. On a 5-day or 6-day split the Shoulders/Arms/Full Body maintenance days are still gym-oriented — a known gap.
Warm-up, rest and HIIT timers keep running on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island.

Log working weight x reps on any exercise (pre-filled from last time), or 'Log each set' for detail. Enter kg or lb. Subscribers can tap 'Snap to fill' to read the weight off a plate, dumbbell, machine display or logbook. Photograph a LOADED BARBELL and it works differently on purpose: no single number in that photo is the lift, so Strathlon lists the plates it read, asks whether that is one end of the bar or every plate on it, lets you set your bar's own weight, and shows the sum written out - plates a side, doubled, plus the bar. The total only reaches the weight field when you tap it. Weights auto-fill next time.

Trained away from the app or your phone? Tap 'Mark this session done' on the plan so it still counts (works for earlier days too). Tap again to undo. Auto-captured sessions (guided or Apple Watch) stay locked.
Collapse/expand workout sections (warm-up, exercises, HIIT finisher) by tapping their headers.
Turn on 'Can double up' so double days train the muscles opposite to those your sport fatigues.

When a plan finishes, Strathlon checks you against your goal: close-but-not-there offers a fresh block sized to what's left; goal hit points to Maintenance; stalled tells you honestly and helps regroup.

sections.name: Logging food & the AI Coach
tips: On the AI Coach tab, tap the camera, photograph your food, then Analyse Photo — or just type what you ate ('two eggs on toast and a flat white'). Either returns a macro estimate with one-tap 'Add to Log'.

From Add to Log, pick the day and meal slot — you can back-date meals up to two weeks. Meal slots are Breakfast, Mid-Morning Snack, Lunch, Afternoon Snack, Dinner and Evening Snack (for anything eaten later in the day) — a food is filed under exactly the slot you tap, including anything the AI Coach logs for you. Logged something under the wrong meal? Tap the … next to any logged item in your Tracker food log — today or a past day — to move it to a different meal slot.

The AI Coach knows your goals, sport, today's targets, logged foods and full programme. Ask 'what should I eat before training?', 'build me a meal plan for today' (returns a full day of meals it saves into Nutrition), or 'how's my progress?'.

To turn a day's food into a shopping list, open the Nutrition tab, scroll past that day type's meals and tap 'Shopping list'. It works from everything on that day — AI-planned meals, food you logged by hand and food you scanned from a photo. It first names every meal the list will cover and marks the ones that carry no ingredients of their own; tap 'Make my list' and your coach estimates those from the meal's name and calories, with every guessed line marked ESTIMATE so you can check it before you shop. The result is a tickable checklist grouped by meal (ticks are saved), and Share sends a clean plain-text list to Apple Reminders, Notes or your grocery app's search — one meal from its own header, or the whole day. There is one list per day type (Training, Rest, Match, Sport, Maintenance). If that day's food changes afterwards — you regenerate the plan, or log another meal — the list offers a 'Refresh list' that rebuilds it and keeps ticks that still match. It's a hand-off to get your list into your shopping app.

The 'Your readiness' card at the top of the AI Coach tab gives you a 0-100 readiness score from your sleep, resting heart rate and between-set recovery. The ring colour alone shows the band (green = well recovered, amber = moderate, red = low); underneath it, one line either reads that band in plain English ('a strong day to train hard' / 'keep it sensible' / 'consider going easier today') or — when it applies — is replaced by a safety caveat instead (a single-signal reliability note, or, on a low or moderate score, that recovery signals can reflect normal cycle variation for women): a caveat always wins over the plain read rather than being appended after it, so it can never be missed. There is a third caveat for a night Strathlon has nothing for: 'No sleep recorded last night - this is your week so far, not today.' It is the SAME test the coach is given, so the card and the coach can never disagree about whether last night exists. When there isn't enough recent Health data yet the card just says 'Your readiness · not enough data yet'. TAPPING the card asks the coach to explain the score in full — the sleep/HR/recovery breakdown and the 'general guide, not medical advice' note now live in that answer, not on the card itself. Explaining the score is a subscriber feature, so a free user is shown the upgrade options instead, and a subscriber who has Health sharing switched off is asked to turn it on first (the coach cannot explain a score it cannot see).

How the readiness score is worked out: it blends three signals - your recent sleep against a 7.5-hour-a-night target, your recent resting heart rate against your OWN baseline rather than a population average, and how far your heart rate drops between sets. Sleep carries about half the weight, resting heart rate about a third, and between-set recovery the rest. The weights stretch to cover whatever data you actually have, so if only sleep and recovery are available the score is built from just those two - and when only ONE signal has enough data the score reflects that signal alone, which the card says in its caveat line. Each signal needs a minimum before it counts - a few nights of sleep, a handful of resting-HR readings, a few rest blocks with heart rate - and a score always needs either sleep or resting heart rate: between-set recovery on its own is not enough, and the card says it hasn't got enough data yet rather than guessing. The exact lookback for each signal is tuned over time, so describe the signals and the weighting rather than quoting a fixed number of days. It is a general guide, not a medical or clinical measure, and it is not comparable with a validated device score. For women, resting-HR and sleep-recovery signals can reflect normal cycle variation - the card only surfaces this as a caveat when the score is momentarily low or moderate, so a ready/green day still shows the daily train-hard steer rather than the caveat.

When you've turned on 'Share Health data with AI coaching' (More → Profile & Settings → App settings → Privacy), the Coach can also see and discuss your Apple Health trends — your sleep in detail (deep/REM/core/awake stages, efficiency and bed/wake times), resting heart rate, heart-rate variability (HRV), respiratory rate, blood oxygen (SpO2), overnight wrist temperature, VO2 max, between-set recovery, weight trend and readiness. It can also see today's movement - steps, walking and running distance, exercise minutes, and your resting-versus-active calorie split - plus how fast your heart rate drops in the minute after training and how your walking heart rate compares with your own normal. If a signal isn't there, or you haven't granted it, the coach is told there is nothing rather than being left to estimate: it is never shown a zero standing in for a missing figure. Just ask 'how's my sleep been?', 'why's my resting HR up?' or 'am I recovered enough to train hard today?'. It reasons only from those figures, never invents numbers, and it's general guidance, not medical advice. Your cycle data has its own separate, off-by-default switch: with it on the coach sees only a general phase label (e.g. 'pre-menstrual'). Your dates, flow and symptoms never leave your phone. With it off, the only cycle-derived thing the coach ever sees is the calorie target itself, and only if the optional pre-period ease is switched on: the number, plus a note that it was deliberately adjusted, never the reason.
Strathlon spots foods you log regularly and offers to auto-add them on chosen days; manage rules under Nutrition → Quick Add (hold a food and choose 'Set as daily auto-add').
Nutrition shows evidence-based supplement guidance tuned to your day type, with dose, timing and why.
The AI Coach (chat, meal plans, photo macro scanning, progress analysis) is premium. Plan, timers, targets, supplements, tracker and Health sync are built in.

If the App Store hasn't confirmed your subscription yet, the top of the AI Coach tab shows a quiet grey line - 'Confirming your subscription. The App Store hasn't confirmed it yet. Your coach stays open while we keep checking' - with a Re-check button. Your access is NOT withdrawn while that says so: Strathlon deliberately holds a subscription it has already confirmed rather than showing a paying member a paywall over a momentary App Store hiccup. It re-checks before your next message rather than letting you find out when a message fails, and if the check comes back negative your typed message is handed back to you instead of being lost. A TestFlight tester will see this fairly often and that is expected - Apple's sandbox subscriptions expire on a fast clock, far quicker than a real one.

sections.name: Tracker, weight & progress
tips: The Tracker's top row shows four tiles — Target, Burned, Consumed, and your Deficit/Surplus/Balance figure (which one depends on your goal — Fat Loss shows Deficit, Muscle Gain/Performance shows Surplus, General Fitness or Maintenance shows Balance). Target is worked out for your day type and updates live when you add activity. Tap the ⓘ on any tile for its source.

Weight from Apple Health is adopted automatically now — there is no "update your weight?" confirm step. What you SEE on the Tracker is always your latest reading; your calorie and protein targets follow a smoothed ~7-day TREND of your weight, so a single heavy or light day doesn't move them. Type a weight in yourself and that entry wins for that day (for about 48 hours). This uses your Apple Health READ permission, which is separate from sharing Health data with the AI Coach.

The weight chart shows actual weight (solid line) plus predicted weight from your tracked calorie deficit or surplus (dashed line, ≈7,700 kcal ≈ 1 kg). They drift apart normally (water, glycogen, adaptation). Premium members can tap 'Ask your coach to explain this gap'. The chart scrolls sideways; rotate or tap ⤢ for full screen with pinch-zoom. Break periods show as a sky-blue band, cycle phases in baby pink. A muted 'Trend' line shows the smoothed ~7-day weight trend that drives your targets.

Open More → Progress Photos to add a photo every week or two (auto-tagged with that day's weight) and tap Compare for before/after. Photos stay on-device by default; optional private-iCloud backup is off by default in More → Profile & Settings → App settings → Privacy & your data.

A 'Your week's ready' card atop the AI Coach tab opens your weekly review (sessions, rest, active burn, energy balance, sleep). One SESSION on that review means one training DAY, however many exercises it contained - a six-exercise gym day counts as one session, not six. The Sessions tile's own info button says the same. Your weight chart lives on the Tracker tab and under Progress → Your Trends, where it shows your whole history rather than one week. Tap 'Ask the Coach about this' to chat with your stats pre-loaded. The top-left 'Progress' pill grows a small dot whenever a new weekly review is ready to read, and inside the menu the item itself reads 'Your Reviews — new', so you can tell which of the two has something new — tap it to open your Past Reviews list, and pick the week from there. Tapping the menu item clears both the dot and the '— new' suffix.

The Strength progress card in your weekly review shows, per exercise: heaviest set, volume-load, a weekly trend arrow, and a deload nudge when a lift stalls. Every figure is a weight you logged - the app does not estimate a one-rep max from your sets, because it never asks you to log rep by rep. Subscribers can also tap 'See full strength history' - next to that card, and in Your Trends (the Progress button, top-left of the AI Coach tab) - to open a per-exercise chart of how a lift has changed over time. That chart plots ONE line: the heaviest single set you logged for that exercise each week, so if you lifted different weights across your sets in a week, the point is the heaviest of them. It marks personal records and shades plateaus, in your chosen weight unit; swipe to scroll your history. Exercises with enough logged weeks to draw a line are listed first in the exercise picker and carry a dot. An exercise with only one logged week shows a short note explaining that a line needs two points, instead of a chart.

On that strength-history chart, once there are at least two logged weeks for that lift (i.e. once a line is actually drawn - below that the chart, its legend, its scrolling note and this button are all replaced by a single-figure state), subscribers can tap 'Analyse my strength' to have your AI coach read that lift's progress - it leads with the trend in the weight you actually lifted (or, for a bodyweight movement with no added load, your total reps) and calls out any personal record or plateau, using only your logged numbers; if there isn't enough history yet it says so and asks you to log a few more sessions rather than guessing, and you can keep chatting from there. The paid weekly review's written analysis also now includes a short strength paragraph (top movers, any PR, any plateau) when you've logged weighted sets.

sections.name: Apple Watch
tips: One-time setup: open the Strathlon app on the watch and tap Allow for Health. You only do this once per watch.

Start a session on the phone and Strathlon starts the workout on the watch automatically — live heart rate streams in and each block logs to Apple's Workout app with calories. No taps needed. A ⌚ shows when it's live.
Do NOT also start Apple's own Workout app for the same session — that double-counts calories.
Heart rate is colour-coded: amber = below target (push harder), red = at/above target.

Premium adds hands-free control: on the wrist, tap Done to log a set and start rest, tap again during rest to skip it - carries you from warm-up through the HIIT finisher. Every one of those buttons WAITS FOR YOUR PHONE: after a tap it shows a spinner until the phone has received, run and acknowledged the command, so a tap that has not landed looks like a tap that has not landed rather than inviting a second one. End and HIIT Stop stay tappable at all times on purpose, so you can always stop a session.
Apple's Fitness app lists workouts by duration, not calories; tap a workout to see calories — they ARE recorded.
No watch? Heart rate still comes from Apple Health where available.

sections.name: Activities, sports & goals
tips: Add a walk, run, cycle, swim, gym class, gym or home workout, or any sport to any day (including rest days) via 'Add activity'. IMPORTANT distinction: logging an activity here RAISES today's eating allowance so you can eat a bit more for it — that's the intake side. Recording the session in Apple Health (an Apple Watch workout, or a manual entry) separately raises the calories Apple Health shows you've BURNED — that's the other side of the same ledger. The two are meant to OFFSET each other, not add together: log the activity here for the eating allowance, and record it in Apple Health too so it also counts toward your burn. Add distance (km) to runs/walks for a sharper estimate; enter your own burn from a watch if you have it.
For gym classes, open Gym classes and search the name (e.g. 'rpm', 'bodypump'); calories scale to your weight and you can tweak duration or pin your own number.

For a gym or home workout, open the 'Gym & home' tile: pick Push/Pull/Leg/Upper day, a full-body/circuit, home bodyweight or home dumbbell — or 'Other workout (custom)'. Search by the name you use ('ppl', 'leg day', 'calisthenics'); calories scale to your weight and duration, or turn on Override to enter your own from a watch. It's for EXTRA or unplanned work — your planned gym session is already counted, so it's never double-counted.
Set each sport's Intensity (Light/Standard/High) in More → Profile & Settings → Sports to tune its calorie bonus. With multiple sports, the primary gets the full bonus and others scale.
When a programme completes, switch to Maintenance: calories rise to full TDEE with carbs raised gradually over a 4-week reverse diet.
Going away? Plan tab → 'On a break or catching up?' pauses your plan (calories ease to maintenance, no deficit, no 'missed day' nagging) and lets you tick days you trained while away.
Change units (kg/lb/stone) in More → Profile & Settings → Body & Stats → Units; everything reflows and saved data is unchanged.

sections.name: Privacy
tips: The 'Share Health data with AI coaching' switch (More -> Profile & Settings -> App settings -> Privacy & your data) covers APPLE HEALTH MEASUREMENTS ONLY: weight, BMI and body composition, metabolic rate (BMR), calories burned and recent deficit, heart rate, heart-rate variability (HRV) and between-set recovery, respiratory rate, blood oxygen (SpO2), overnight wrist temperature, cardio fitness (VO2 max), recent off-app workouts, today's steps, walking and running distance and exercise minutes, the split between resting and active calories burned, one-minute heart-rate recovery after training and walking heart rate compared with your own baseline, your sleep in detail (total sleep and sleep debt, the deep/REM/core/awake breakdown, sleep efficiency, and your bed and wake times), weight history, the derived readiness score, AND the user's hormone-therapy status if they have set one (shared so the coach reasons from their actual logged data rather than a sex-typical baseline). It is off by default; turning it off keeps all of those on the phone. It does NOT control the health & safety details the user typed in - see the next tip.

The health & safety details the user TYPED IN THEMSELVES are always shared with the AI Coach on every message and are NOT controlled by the 'Share Health data' switch: allergies and supplements to avoid, pregnancy and breastfeeding, chronic conditions, medications, and injuries. This is deliberate - a coach that does not know about an allergy, a pregnancy or a heart medication could give unsafe advice. If a user asks what the coach knows about them, say this plainly; never tell them these details are withheld.

Food preferences are also always shared with the coach, including dietary or religious preferences such as halal, kosher, vegetarian or vegan, plus preferred cuisines and cooking time, so meal ideas suit the user.
Users can see the full list any time: More -> Profile & Settings -> App settings -> Privacy & your data -> 'What your AI coach can see'.

What happens to the data sent to the AI: to keep follow-up questions fast, the AI provider briefly caches the BACKGROUND CONTEXT we send (a few minutes); beyond that our processors apply only their own limited operational retention, such as short-term abuse prevention. Strathlon keeps no long-term store of messages. Do NOT tell a user their messages are simply 'discarded' - that overstates what we know. If someone asks whether their data is sold, used for advertising or used to train AI models, point them to the privacy policy and to the consent screen shown during onboarding rather than answering it from here.

Cycle-aware coaching is a separate, off-by-default switch; if on, the coach sees only a general phase label (e.g. 'pre-menstrual'). Your dates, flow and symptoms never leave your phone. One thing does not depend on that switch: the optional 'Ease my targets in my pre-period week' option (also off by default) adds about 100 kcal to the Nutrition target around the period, and the coach sees that adjusted target plus a note that it was deliberately adjusted - never that the cycle is the reason, unless the phase-share switch is also on. Cycle features are also stood DOWN by default for a biological-female user who has told us they are on testosterone therapy, because periods commonly stop or become irregular on masculinising therapy; an 'I still menstruate' toggle in More -> Profile & Settings -> Cycle-aware insights turns them straight back on.

Biological sex is ALWAYS shared with the AI Coach, alongside name and age, because the calorie model cannot be explained without it - it is shared as a number-driving fact and nothing more. HORMONE THERAPY is different: it is treated as sensitive health data, so it only reaches the coach when the 'Share Health data with AI coaching' switch is on. It is also left OUT of the iCloud backup unless the separate, off-by-default 'Back up health & safety details' switch is on. Setting it back to 'None' in Body & stats removes it everywhere.

The tracker mirrors food logs, saved foods and auto-add rules to your private iCloud (no Strathlon account, raw meals never uploaded to Strathlon); turn off in More -> Profile & Settings -> App settings -> Privacy & your data.

The default-ON 'iCloud backup' switch includes basic details, weight, daily totals, goals, training setup, plan progress AND food preferences - including any dietary or religious preference set, such as halal or kosher. It does NOT include health & safety details, and it does NOT include allergies; those have their own separate, off-by-default switch ('Back up health & safety details').
Suggest and vote on features via More -> 'App roadmap & Feedback'.

sections.name: Onboarding & your profile in detail
tips: You don't need an account, sign-up or password — your profile, logs and full history live on your device, so nothing to remember and nothing to lose to a forgotten password.

First-run setup builds the plan around you: your body details, your goal, your sport (pick from any category across 38 sports), and your weekly training/match schedule. You can edit these later in More → Profile & Settings. To change your goal or experience there are two routes and they run the IDENTICAL flow, both keeping all your logged history: More → Profile & Settings → 'Goal & plan' → 'Change goal or experience' → 'Redo onboarding' (the route most people find, since that is where the goal is displayed), or More → Profile & Settings → Reset & Data → 'Restart and redo onboarding'. A backup is made automatically first.

Manage your data in More → Profile & Settings → Reset & Data. RESTART: 'Restart my plan' puts your plan back to Week 1 today (keeps all history), and 'Restart and redo onboarding' lets you change your goal or experience (also keeps history). CLEAR SPECIFIC DATA: tick just what you want gone — Nutrition log, Weight & body, Lifting history, Holiday periods, Coach conversations or Cycle data — everything is off by default. What you clear goes from this device and from your private iCloud backup; your Coach conversations live only on this device, so clearing them removes the only copy. Two buckets keep something on purpose, and the app says so on screen: 'Weight & body' keeps measurements logged without a weight (a waist or chest entry on its own), and 'Lifting history' keeps the record of which exercises were ticked off each day. DELETE EVERYTHING: type DELETE to erase all your data and your iCloud backup and start fresh — that includes your saved foods, auto-add rules, saved meal plans, schedule changes, profile photo, any stored voice key, and (from build 211) your weight-stack photos, any data export you made, your saved shopping lists, the coach's notes on your progress photos and the record of which exercises you ticked off on which day. Nothing is copied back afterwards, and if anything cannot be removed the app tells the user rather than reporting a clean wipe. ONE EXCEPTION, stated on both delete screens: workouts Strathlon saved to Apple Health stay in Apple's Health app — they are the user's and they live in Apple's app, so delete them from Health if they want them gone. Clearing Cycle data asks a second time and never touches Apple Health. It cannot be undone and Strathlon keeps no hidden recoverable copy, so use 'Export my data first' (a CSV + JSON copy) at the top of that screen before you clear or delete.

The readiness check is a short, optional set of yes/no questions — the kind a trainer asks before you start. If an answer stands out, Strathlon gently suggests getting medical clearance first. It is a readiness check, not medical advice. The individual answers stay on-device; the coach is told only that a readiness item was flagged (and whether clearance was confirmed), so it can keep guidance conservative.

The health & safety step captures pregnancy/breastfeeding, ongoing conditions, medications, allergies, and any food or supplement ingredients to avoid. Your allergies and avoid-ingredients go to the Coach as a hard exclusion on every message, so meal plans are built to leave them out.
You are asked ONCE whether the AI Coach may see your Apple Health figures. It is off by default and can be changed any time in More → Profile & Settings → App settings → Privacy & your data.

To edit anything later: More → Profile & Settings. 'Body & stats' holds your measurements, your units and the 'Week starts on' preference. YOUR GOAL WEIGHT IS EDITABLE ON ITS OWN (build 213) - More → Profile & Settings → 'Goal & plan' → the 'GOAL WEIGHT' section - so NEVER tell a user to redo onboarding just to change their target weight. Your GOAL ITSELF (fat loss / muscle gain / general fitness / sports performance) and your EXPERIENCE LEVEL are different and remain read-only wherever they are shown, because they reshape the whole plan - change those via 'Goal & plan' → 'Change goal or experience' → 'Redo onboarding', or via Reset & Data → 'Restart and redo onboarding' (the same flow either way, and history is kept). The Health-data sharing switch is under App settings → Privacy & your data, and cycle-phase sharing under HEALTH → Cycle-aware insights.

Resting heart rate and VO2 max are optional in setup and must be realistic to be accepted: resting HR between 30 and 150 bpm, VO2 max between 10 and 100 ml/kg/min. If you enter something outside that it is not saved -- and if you already had a value saved, that one is kept -- and the field tells you which happened. You can change both later without redoing setup: More -> Profile & Settings -> Body & stats has a Resting HR and a VO2 max stepper. Your five heart-rate zones appear under More -> Profile & Settings -> Your targets, worked out from your age-based maximum HR and your resting HR. If a value saved by an older version is outside the plausible range, the zones are worked out from a default of 60 bpm and a note above them says so. If the gap between your resting HR and your maximum is too small to give meaningful zones, the ladder is replaced by a note explaining that. Either way, adjust your resting HR in Body & stats to fix it.

BMR AND HORMONE THERAPY. Strathlon works out BMR in one of TWO ways, and Profile -> Your targets -> 'BMR formula' always names which one is running. (1) If a measured body-fat % or lean mass is available (body composition switched ON), BMR comes from that MEASURED value via Katch-McArdle - the most accurate route, and it always wins regardless of any hormone-therapy answer; a user who has body composition switched OFF stays on branch (2) no matter what they answer on hormone therapy. (2) Otherwise BMR is the standard weight-based Mifflin-St Jeor estimate from weight, height, age and biological sex - the equation itself is NEVER swapped - and if the user is on hormone therapy a bounded kcal adjustment is added on top: body-fat is estimated from height, weight and age for the user's biological sex, shifted HALF of the way toward the body composition that therapy tends to produce, clamped to a physiological range, and the resulting change in implied lean mass is converted into a kcal delta. COUNTER-INTUITIVE CASE: for a user whose therapy pushes in the SAME direction their birth sex already sits (a male-born user on testosterone, a female-born user on estrogen), that shift is clamped out entirely and the delta is EXACTLY ZERO - their calories are byte-identical to what they'd be without answering the hormone question, so never tell a user in this case that their estimate was 'shifted'. The 'BMR formula' row reads one of three values: 'Katch-McArdle' (measured), 'Weight-based (hormone-adjusted)' (branch 2 with a non-zero delta applied), or 'Weight-based' (branch 2, no delta, including everyone not on hormone therapy). 'Katch-McArdle (estimated)' no longer exists as a value - never use it. Adding a real body-fat % in Body & stats always replaces any weight-based estimate. The minimum daily calorie floor is keyed to biological sex and the hormone adjustment can never push a user below it. Tap the info icon next to Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) in Your targets for the same explanation in plain English.

GOAL WEIGHT EDITOR (build 213). More → Profile & Settings → 'Goal & plan' → 'GOAL WEIGHT'. It is the SAME stepper, the same three warning banners and the same rules as the last screen of onboarding - one shared component, not a second copy - so advice given about one is true of the other. Underneath the stepper it states what the target means: how far there is to go, how many training weeks remain in the plan, and the weekly rate that implies. IF THE PACE IS FASTER THAN A STEADY ONE IT SAYS SO AND STILL LETS THE USER SAVE - a target is a goal, not a schedule, so do not treat that message as a block. The ONLY thing that disables 'Save goal weight' is a target that CONTRADICTS the goal (a fat-loss target above current weight, or a gain target below it); the button also stays disabled when nothing has actually been changed, and reads 'Saved' once a target is stored and untouched. Changing the goal weight re-derives goal progress, the end-of-plan branch and the 'X to go' line, and it does NOT rebuild the plan, does NOT change calories, macros or the deficit, and does NOT re-anchor where the journey started - the distance already covered is kept.

WEEK STARTS ON (build 213). More → Profile & Settings → 'Body & stats' → 'Week starts on' - a Sun / Mon choice, DEFAULT SUNDAY. It changes which day the Plan tab's THIS WEEK strip and the sport calendar begin on, and both move together. IT IS A DISPLAY SETTING ONLY, and this is the part to get right when asked: WEEKLY REVIEWS AND TRAINING STREAKS ALWAYS RUN MONDAY TO SUNDAY whichever way this is set, so flipping it never relabels a week already trained and never changes a past review. The weekly schedule the user set in onboarding is unaffected - a Wednesday gym day is still Wednesday; only which seven dates the strip spans changes. The AI coach reads the week the same way round as the Plan tab does, so 'this week' means the same seven days in the chat as on screen.

sections.name: Running a workout, timers & supersets
tips: The workout screen is split into fold-out sections — warm-up, your main workout, and a HIIT finisher. Warm-up and HIIT start folded to cut scrolling; your main workout stays open. Tap any header to collapse or expand it.

Warm-up, rest and HIIT countdowns keep running on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island with spoken cues, so you can put the phone down between sets. The voice coach calls each exercise and set including the rep target, with a 3-2-1 into each work set.

Some training days end with a HIIT finisher and a short core finisher (such as plank, dead bug or glute bridge march). It tops up to 2 core moves for the day in total, counting any core work your sport accessories already include — so it may add 0, 1 or 2 moves — and it never repeats the same movement pattern (e.g. rotational) twice. Core is added on strength days only — not on rest, sport-only or maintenance days — and it rotates week to week. A gym-plus-sport double day IS a strength day, so it does get core work: any core your sport accessories already cover counts toward the day's two slots, so such a day often needs only one extra move, or none.

Both the HIIT finisher and the core finisher adapt to any injury you flag. HIIT filters its movements for all injury types (a shoulder injury hides overhead and forceful-arm moves; a lower-back injury hides jumps, hinges and crunches; an elbow injury hides gripping moves; knee/ankle keep the low-impact set), always leaving at least six safe options, and shows an 'Adapted for:' banner. The core finisher likewise only ever shows core work that is safe for your injuries.
Log working weight × reps on any exercise (pre-filled from last time), or choose 'Log each set' for per-set detail. Enter kg or lb. Bodyweight moves can be saved with a weight of 0.

Subscribers can tap 'Snap to fill' to photograph a dumbbell, plate or machine display and Strathlon reads the number off it. A LOADED BARBELL is handled differently, because no single figure in that photo is the weight you lifted: Strathlon shows the plates it read, a one-tap choice between 'one end of the bar' and 'every plate on the bar', your bar's own weight (20 kg unless you change it, and it remembers), and the arithmetic line by line. Nothing goes into the weight field until you tap the total, and nothing is saved until you tap Save. Weights then auto-fill next time, so you just confirm or nudge them.

Where the plan pairs exercises into groups, each group header has its own switch. Leave it on to run that group back-to-back as a superset/tri-set; turn it off to do those exercises one at a time as straight sets, each with its own start button and rest between every set. The app remembers the choice per pairing, so a combination that never works at your gym stays as straight sets. On a switched-off group, tap the info button on its header for how to keep the same training density.

Trained away from the app or your phone? Tap 'Mark this session done' so it still counts (works for earlier days too); tap again to undo. Sessions captured automatically (a guided session or an Apple Watch workout) stay locked so real training is never removed by accident.

HOW A DAY IS BALANCED, AND THE PHASE-1 CEILING (build 213). Three rules are applied to the WHOLE ASSEMBLED DAY - the gym lifts, the sport accessories and the core finisher together, not just the gym block: (1) no two exercises in the day train the same movement pattern; (2) a day that presses must also carry a ROW and a PULLDOWN OR CHIN; (3) pulling sets must reach at least 80% of pressing sets. Where the user's equipment or the day genuinely cannot supply a missing movement, the rule STANDS DOWN and leaves the exercise that was already there - a session is never made SHORTER to satisfy a rule. A dedicated Push day balances against its paired Pull day rather than within itself, which is what a push/pull split is for. The FIRST exercise of the day never changes, because that is the lift strength progress is tracked on, and when a sport accessory collides with a gym movement it is the SPORT move that is swapped, not the main lift. SEPARATELY, PHASE 1 (Reactivation) IS CAPPED AT 8 EXERCISES for the whole assembled day - roughly 24 working sets - because it is the easing-back-in block; sport accessories and the core finisher are NEVER what gets cut, only the main lifts are trimmed, and the trim keeps the press, the row, the pulldown and the leg work in preference to isolation. A phase-1 user with NO sport is normally under the ceiling already and sees no change. PHASES 2 AND 3 ARE NOT CAPPED. None of this changes calorie burn: burn is worked out separately from the displayed session duration.

sections.name: The weight chart & energy-balance in detail
tips: The weight chart plots your ACTUAL weight as a solid line and your PREDICTED weight (from your tracked calorie deficit or surplus, at roughly 7,700 kcal per kg) as a dashed line. A third muted 'Trend' line is the smoothed ~7-day weight trend Strathlon uses to set your calorie and protein targets. Reading them together shows whether real change is tracking the maths.
The two lines drift apart normally — real weight often drops faster at first from water and glycogen, then the prediction can run ahead as your body adapts. That divergence is expected, not an error.
Tap the expand button or rotate to landscape for a full-screen chart with pinch-zoom and a drag crosshair. The chart scrolls sideways through your history.
Break periods show as a sky-blue band and, if cycle-aware coaching is on, cycle phases show in baby pink — so context around a plateau is visible at a glance.
Premium members can tap 'Ask your coach to explain this gap' to open a chat with the numbers pre-loaded; the coach usually asks a question or two before explaining rather than guessing.

The Tracker's four top tiles are Target, Burned, Consumed and your Deficit, Surplus or Balance figure (whichever matches your goal). Target is computed for your day type and updates live as you add activity. Tap the info icon on any tile to see exactly where its number comes from.

sections.name: History, export & data ownership
tips: Open Tracker → History for your daily log, newest first — calories in, calories out and weight for each day.

Missed a day? Tracker → History → 'Add missed day', pick the date, then fill in calories consumed and burned (burned is pulled from Apple Health where it has data) and optionally a weight. The calendar covers yesterday and earlier — today is edited on the Tracker screen itself, where the burn is live from Apple Health (whichever device or app writes it there — an Apple Watch if you wear one, otherwise your iPhone's motion sensors). When Apple Health has no burn data for today at all, the Burned and Deficit/Surplus/Balance tiles show a dash rather than a zero, so no deficit or surplus is implied.

Picking a date you have ALREADY logged is safe: the sheet switches to 'Edit Day', shows what that day currently holds, and arrives with your saved values already filled in. Saving updates only the boxes shown — your logged food items and your protein/carbs/fat are always kept. Leaving a box empty means 'leave that value as it is', not zero.
To correct just a weigh-in for a past day, open 'Add missed day' for that date and change only the weight — the calorie boxes can be left empty.
Use Import / Export in History for a CSV round-trip of your daily log, so your data is portable and yours to keep.

Because you don't sign in, everything lives on-device by default. In More → Profile & Settings → App settings → Privacy & your data you control each backup separately: 'iCloud backup' (on by default) covers your basic details, weight, daily totals, goals, training setup, plan progress and food preferences - including any dietary or religious preference such as halal, kosher, vegetarian or vegan; 'Back up training data to iCloud' (ON by default) covers your weigh-ins and lifting history; 'Back up health & safety details' and 'Sync progress photos to iCloud' are each OFF by default and cover your allergies/injuries/conditions and your progress photos respectively. All backups go to your own private iCloud only, never a Strathlon server. Cycle data is never included in any of them.

Raw meals and photos are never uploaded to Strathlon's servers. Strathlon reads the figures the user permits and writes nothing back from the phone; if they use Strathlon on an Apple Watch, the watch app saves the workouts it records to Apple Health - that is the only thing Strathlon writes.
Change units (kg / lb / stone) any time in More → Profile & Settings → Body & Stats → Units; the whole app reflows and your saved data is unchanged underneath.

If you reinstall or move to a new phone and restore your backup, your health & safety details will NOT come back unless you had turned 'Back up health & safety details' on — it is off by default. Strathlon warns you before you restore and keeps a reminder at the top of your Profile until you re-enter them, because until you do, your meals and plan cannot take your allergies, injuries, conditions or medications into account.

sections.name: Notifications, nuggets & learning
tips: A daily knowledge nugget card surfaces a short, evidence-based tip; some nuggets carry a 'Learn more' link that opens a fuller article on strathlon.com.

Two local notifications are ON by default, controlled in More → Profile & Settings → App settings → Notifications & Tips: 'Daily tip notification' (one science-backed tip each morning, around 9am) and 'Bedtime reminder' (a gentle nightly wind-down reminder, with extra recovery emphasis after a hard training day, around 10:45pm). Notification permission is asked once, near the end of onboarding — if declined, both stay switched on in Settings but won't actually notify until permission is granted (Settings app → Notifications → Strathlon), and Strathlon never re-prompts automatically.

The weekly review card ('Your week's ready') sits atop the AI Coach tab and opens a summary of sessions, rest, active burn, energy balance and sleep (your weight chart is on the Tracker tab and under Progress → Your Trends). Tap 'Ask the Coach about this' to chat with those stats pre-loaded.

The top-left 'Progress' pill atop the AI Coach tab shows a small unread dot when a new weekly review is ready, and opening the menu tells you which of its two items is new: the entry reads 'Your Reviews — new' ('Your Trends' never carries a marker). Tap it to open your Past Reviews list — a browsable journal of every week and month generated, newest first — and pick the review from there; tapping the menu item clears both the dot and the '— new' suffix. There's no separate progress-analysis card to check any more.

Deeper guides and evidence articles live on the website — the Learn library, per-stat explainer pages, and topic guides (building muscle, fat loss, training with your cycle, supplements, recovery, habits). Ask the Coach and it can point you to the relevant one.
